newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends sharply lower as funds sell.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends sharply lower as funds sell.

text.p: Technically-driven fund selling and a dearth of buying interest pressured CSCE world sugar futures to settle sharply weaker and barely above the day's lows, market sources said.
The selling accelerated once March fell under 10.55 and then 10.34, both viewed as key support levels.
"This was purely technical. March failed to get over a previous high...hit stops and there were no buyers to buoy it up," Refco analyst Ann Prendergast, said.
The most-active March contract ended below support pegged at 10.34, the recent low made Nov 18, and slightly above a one-month low of 10.21, made Nov 6.
The March life-of-contract low is 9.48 cents a lb.
March closed the session down 0.39 to 10.27, traded 10.65 to 10.23. The back months settled 0.32 to 0.25 lower.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 32,256 lots.
Resistance remained at 10.70 cents in March.
While today's losses were technically-inspired, additional weakness could result from a lack of offtake amid ample world supplies.
"Fundamentally, reports of surplus production between 3 million and 7 million tonnes has been a burdening factor which has restrained advances," Prendergast said.
German statistician F.O. Licht said Friday that world sugar stocks could rise sharply from year-ago levels, as output in major exporting nations is seen rising.
Licht put world production at 123.95 million tonnes for 1996/97, in an October estimate. Surplus stocks could climb to 6 million tonnes this crop year
But the market is oversold technically, and prices are seen recouping some losses Wednesday, dealers said.
